full_judgment:
6. Wazed brought a suit for recovery of possession against Julekha, in 1933 and got decree to that effect. Then Julekha preferred an appeal and after disposal of the said appeal Julekha filed a Review Case being No. 3 of 1933 which was ultimately ended on compromise and in terms of compromise Julekha got the share of Wazed. Shahar Ali transferred his 0.07 acres of land to Julekha by a registered kabala dated 8-8-1943. Thereafter Julekha died leaving behind her husband Saimuddin and mother Hemela Khatun. Hemela had no son and thus she took one Jalil as her adopted son. Hemela gifted her share to the said adopted son by a registered deed dated 28-2-1953. By that way Saimuddin and jalil were while owning and possessing the suit land, they settled the same to this defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun by a patta dated 11-2-1955. The defendant Mosammat Saleha Khatun by this way while has been owning and possessing the suit land since the date of the settlement made and at the time in SA operation the suit land was thus recorded in her name. The plaintiff has/had no title and possession over the suit land and, as such, she shought for dismissal of the suit. 

 19. In other words the defendant's claim was that Rafiudddin and Shahar Ali in their turn got 0.07 acres of land from their mother who by amicable arrangement developed the same in favour of the Shahar Ali who sold out the same by a registered deed dated 8-8-1943 in favour of Julekha, the daughter of Hamid Molla's son and upon her demise the part of said property developed in favour of her mother Hemela Khatun who had no son and thus she adopted a son namely Jalil and then she gifted her full share to Jalil by a gift deed dated 28-2-1953. The said Jalil on 11-2-1955 by a Patta transferred the same to the present defendant, Saleha Khatun and upon such chain of title the defendant obtained the suit land by the deed of transfer as above. The SA record was thus rightly published in the name of the defendant Saleha Khatun who thus succeed in the suit upto the appellate Court. Even though she ultimately died but her legal heirs and representatives are therefore substituted and contested in her place in the present Rule.
